adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:123 — [P1, confidence 100] The Prometheus-only list path computes `canPause` from `grafanaPauseAbility` but the menu renders Pause only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`, so authorized users lose the pause/restore action after ruler-rule preloading is removed.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for AlertRuleMenu.tsx, the Pause menu item rendering logic at line 123 checks `canPause` which is now computed as `(pauseSupported && pauseAllowed) || (grafanaPauseSupported && grafanaPauseAllowed)`. This means if either the ruler-based OR the grafana-prom-based ability check passes, canPause will be true. The finding claims users 'lose the pause/restore action' but the code shows the opposite - the OR logic ensures that when rulerRule is not available (skipToken case), the grafanaPauseAbility can still enable the pause action. The menu item visibility depends on canPause, not on rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) for the pause action specifically.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for AlertRuleMenu.tsx, the Delete menu item rendering logic is not shown in the diff - only the ability computation is shown. The finding claims 'the menu renders Delete only when rulerRule exists' but this rendering logic is not visible in the diff. The diff shows that canDelete is computed as an OR of both ruler and grafana abilities: `canDelete = (deleteSupported && deleteAllowed) || (grafanaDeleteSupported && grafanaDeleteAllowed)`. This means if grafana abilities allow deletion, canDelete will be true. Without seeing the actual menu rendering code in the diff, we cannot verify the claim that Delete is only rendered when rulerRule exists. The finding makes an assumption about code not shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/components/RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:104 — `[rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer]` prevents the silence drawer from rendering for the new promRule-only list items after `handleSilence={() => setShowSilenceDrawer(true)}` reports the menu action as available, so clicking “Silence notifications” performs no user-visible operation (P1, confidence 100).

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx, the silence drawer rendering condition at line 104 is `{rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer && <SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer...}`. The finding claims this prevents the drawer from rendering for promRule-only items. However, examining the code: (1) The `rule` parameter is now optional (`rule?: RulerRuleDTO`), (2) The SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer receives `rulerRule={rule!}` which would be undefined for promRule-only cases, but (3) The AlertRuleMenu component that calls `handleSilence` uses `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` to check if silence is allowed based on promRule, and the canSilence check in AlertRuleMenu.tsx combines both ruler and grafana abilities. The actual issue would be that when rule is undefined, `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` returns false, preventing the drawer. But looking at the AlertRuleMenu, it passes `rulerRule={undefined}` to the menu, and the silence action availability is determined by the combined check. The finding's specific line reference (104) and the exact condition don't match what's shown in the diff - the diff shows the condition spans lines 103-108. More importantly, the finding assumes the silence menu item would be shown but the drawer wouldn't render, but this requires verifying the full flow which isn't clearly broken in the diff.

Looking at the test's ui.menuItems selectors and the assertions, the test explicitly checks for silence, copyLink, duplicate, and export - there is no assertion for delete in this test.
